title: Zero a dial comparator on a gauge block, then measure and sort three spacers
instruction: Zero the dial on the master block by turning its bezel, put the master back on its yellow MASTER area, then measure each spacer under the dial and sort it: within 25.00 +- 0.02 mm into ACCEPT, otherwise into REJECT.
context: Checking parts against a set master with a dial indicator or comparator is routine dimensional inspection. O*NET (2025) counts 602,000 inspectors, testers and sorters and 288,300 machinists, 890,300 together; measuring parts for conformance with precision instruments is a core task of both, and the inspectors' task list names dial indicators. No public count isolates comparator users; the README gives the sources and the reasoning.
setup: On the bench: a cast iron dial comparator stand (KBC 1-807-450 type: enamelled cast iron base 3-7/8 x 6 in, long side front to back, centre x 0.42, y -0.05 m, raised serrated steel anvil 60 mm across and 10 mm proud of the base under the contact, 8 in tall; 1 in round steel column 65 mm behind the dial, 205 mm tall). The arm is locked on the column (column clamp knob on its side, fine-adjust knob on top, indicator stem clamp at its front end; none is used). It holds a 0.01 mm dial indicator (Mitutoyo 2046A type, held by its lug back: 57 mm dial facing the robots, knurled bezel about 60 mm across that turns the face and its 0 mark, 10 mm travel, flat 6 mm contact point accessory) over the anvil. At the start the bezel is turned so the seated master reads -0.06 mm. A spindle lifting lever (40 mm, at the top of the indicator spindle, pointing away from the dial) raises the contact when its end is pressed down. Left of the stand, a parts tray (blue plastic, 209 x 70 mm, 6 mm rims, a marked spot per part, centre x 0.42, y -0.17) holds, on a yellow area marked MASTER (33 x 50 mm, at its left end), the setting master: a 25.000 mm steel rectangular gauge block (35 x 9 mm, at x 0.33) with a yellow painted band and "MASTER 25.000" printed on its side, and, on marked spots between low printed ribs, three steel spacers cut from ground flat stock (40 x 10 mm footprint, chamfered edges, a small through-bore near one end, long side along y, at x 0.39, 0.44 and 0.49, painted 1, 2 and 3 on the side). Their heights look the same; which are within 25.00 +- 0.02 mm depends on the trial seed (8 seeds, one per good/bad pattern). Simulated heights are exact examples (25.01/25.00/24.99 mm in tolerance, 25.04/25.04/24.96 mm out). Before physical trials each blank is measured with a 0-1 in micrometer and classed from that reading; a blank within 0.005 mm of a limit is not used. In front of the stand, two moulded open bins 100 x 80 x 15 mm, each with its name printed on the bench in front of it: ACCEPT (green rims, centre x 0.26, y -0.20) and REJECT (red rims, x 0.26, y -0.29). The bezel carries two red tolerance markers at +-0.02 mm that turn with it.
scoring: 1.0: the dial was zeroed by turning the bezel while the master was under the contact (after the fingers open, the master reads within one 0.01 mm division of 0), each spacer rested under the released contact for at least 0.5 s, every spacer is in the right bin (25.00 +- 0.02 mm in ACCEPT, the rest in REJECT), the master's whole footprint is back inside its yellow MASTER area and has not moved more than 2 mm in any direction or tilted more than 3 deg since, both hands are at least 80 mm from every part and the dial, and everything is still for 1 s. 0.5: the same with exactly two spacers measured and in the right bin (so three measured with one in the wrong bin scores 0.5). 0 otherwise, including: the master left in a bin or anywhere outside its MASTER area, or moved more than 2 mm in any direction or tilted more than 3 deg after its return; the zero not set, set on a spacer, or set with nothing under the contact; a part off the bench; a hand within 80 mm; motion at the end.
reset_notes: Turn the bezel back to its start mark (the master reads -0.06 mm), put the parts back in their marked spots and empty both bins. Seeds 0-7 set which spacers are in tolerance; evaluation seeds are withheld from the controller. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at stock sizes. The needle is driven only by the contact's real travel (1 mm per turn, 0.01 mm divisions); the bezel is a hinged ring turned by fingertip contact. The lever lifts the spindle 0.05 mm per mrad. Estimated: bezel friction, base thickness, spindle spring 150 N/m, lever length, spacer sizes. The simulated spacer heights are exact; real pieces use their measured heights.
